title: AI Phone Assistant: Humans Appear Behind the Scenes
part1: You can ask AI to make phone calls. When you hear that, you might picture a future phone assistant smoothly taking care of requests. But in a feature Meta tested through Muse, AI did not make some of the calls. Trained contract workers called people on users’ behalf and handled the conversations. Human workers appeared behind the scenes of AI phone calls. It was a turn of events that makes you want to check the cast list again.
part2:
But this is not just a story about thinking it was AI and finding out it was a person. Explaining the reason for a call may require information about the user. Employees at the company worried that if contract workers handled the calls, sensitive information might be shared by mistake.

Here the story changes from a comparison of AI performance to a story about privacy. The problem is not that a person makes the call. What matters to users is knowing who is making the call and who might get their information. This is not a story about a large-scale leak of information. The concern was about a way of running the service that could lead to information being shared with people.
part3:
A Meta executive admitted that it was a mistake to start the test without a proper explanation. The company then paused the human concierge feature for now. It did not stop Muse as a whole.

If AI only answers on a screen, you may not think about what happens behind the scenes. But when it makes phone calls, you start to wonder whether there is a person there and what information is being passed along. The arrival of human workers was an unexpected casting choice, and it also showed that even behind the scenes of convenience, an explanation is needed.
in_one_line: Meta’s AI phone-call test used human contractors, raising concerns about who might receive users’ personal information.
